title: Apollo 15 lost one of its three parachutes on the way down. It only needed two

cover.alt: Seen from high above, the Apollo 15 capsule hangs under two open parachutes over a dark blue sea, with a third parachute collapsed into a thin streamer beside them.

body: On 7 August 1971, Apollo 15’s command module came home under three main parachutes, each 83 feet (25 m) wide, which opened about 10,000 feet (3,000 m) above the Pacific. At around 6,000 feet one of them collapsed, most likely because leftover fuel the capsule was dumping overboard damaged its risers and lines. The crew were never in danger, because the landing system was **designed to set the capsule down safely on just two parachutes**: the third was a spare. With one canopy gone the capsule hit the water a little harder than planned, about 330 miles (530 km) north of Honolulu, and the astronauts were unhurt.

slides.alt: Seen from above, a small capsule hangs beneath two open pale parachutes over a dark blue sea, while a third parachute trails beside them collapsed into a narrow streamer. The capsule drops lower until it hits the water in a white splash.
slides.caption: 7 August 1971: Apollo 15 drops towards the Pacific under two full parachutes while the third flaps beside them, collapsed, until the capsule splashes down.

steps.label: 24,000 ft: two drogues slow it to 170 mph

slides.question: On two parachutes instead of three, how fast did Apollo 15 hit the water?
slides.explanation: About 22 mph (35 km/h). With all three parachutes, NASA expected about 19 mph: a firmer splash, but the crew were not harmed.

slides.label: the peak force on the crew as the capsule braked in the upper air
slides.text: The capsule, Endeavour, met the atmosphere at about 24,580 mph (39,600 km/h), and radio contact was cut off for about three and a half minutes.

slides.question: What most likely damaged Apollo 15’s failed parachute?
slides.explanation: During the descent the capsule dumped its leftover thruster fuel overboard, and that most likely damaged the parachute’s risers and suspension lines.

source.label: NASA: Apollo 15, Home from the Moon
